name: ADG733BRUZ-REEL7
title: Low-voltage CMOS triple and quad SPDT switches, 2.5 Ω
summary: The ADG733 holds three SPDT switches and the ADG734 four, each a 2:1 selector with a few ohms of on resistance, flat across the signal range. They run from one supply of 1.8 V to 5.5 V or from ±2.5 V, pass signals in either direction between the rails, and draw about a nanoamp. The ADG733 steers its switches with three address lines and has an active-low enable that opens every channel; the ADG734 has one logic input per switch. Switching is break-before-make.
key_figures: 1.8 V to 5.5 V single, or ±2.5 V dual
2.5 Ω typ, 5.0 Ω max (VDD = 5 V, -40 °C to +85 °C)

circuits.title: Test Circuit 1. On resistance
circuits.description: A current source forces IDS through the closed switch while S sits at the test level VS; the voltage V1 across the switch divided by IDS gives RON.

circuits.title: Test Circuit 2. IS (OFF)
circuits.description: The switch is open. VS biases the source through an ammeter and VD biases the drain; the ammeter reads the source off leakage.

circuits.title: Test Circuit 3. ID (ON)
circuits.description: The switch is closed and its source left open. VD biases the drain through an ammeter, which reads the channel on leakage.

circuits.title: Test Circuit 4. Switching times, tON and tOFF
circuits.description: Switch 1 has a different DC level on each source and a 300 Ω, 35 pF load on its drain. A pulse on the logic input flips the switch; tON and tOFF run from the 50% point of the logic edge to the 90% point of the output.
notes: The logic input is labelled IN/EN: an address line on the ADG733, an IN pin on the ADG734.

circuits.title: Test Circuit 5. Enable delay, tON(EN) and tOFF(EN)
circuits.description: All three ADG733 address lines are grounded, so switch 1 selects S1A, which carries the test level; S1B is grounded. A pulse source with a 50 Ω termination drives EN, and the drain feeds 300 Ω with 35 pF. The delays run from the 50% point of the EN edge to 90% of the output level.
notes: Enable drive swings 0 V to 3 V.

circuits.title: Test Circuit 6. Break-before-make delay, tOPEN
circuits.description: Both sources of one switch are tied to the same test level, so the output only dips while neither side is closed. A 0 V to 3 V pulse with a 50 Ω termination drives the address input; tOPEN is the gap between the 80% points of the output dip.
notes: The address drive is A0, A1 or A2 on the ADG733 and IN1 to IN4 on the ADG734.

circuits.title: Test Circuit 7. Charge injection
circuits.description: A DC source with series resistance RS feeds the switch; the drain is loaded only by 1 nF. Toggling the enable (IN on the ADG734) between 0 V and 3 V makes a step ΔVOUT on the capacitor, and the injected charge is CL times that step.

circuits.title: Test Circuit 8. Off isolation
circuits.description: With the switch held open by its logic input, a network analyser drives the source through 50 Ω, the source is terminated in 50 Ω at the chip, and the drain goes to the analyser's 50 Ω input. Off isolation is 20 log(VOUT/VS). Both leads are coaxial with grounded shields.

circuits.title: Test Circuit 9. Channel-to-channel crosstalk
circuits.description: The analyser drives SB, the closed side, through 50 Ω, and the drain is terminated in 50 Ω. The open side SA goes to the analyser input with a 50 Ω load. Crosstalk is 20 log(VOUT/VS). Both leads are coaxial with grounded shields.

circuits.title: Test Circuit 10. Bandwidth
circuits.description: With the switch closed, the analyser drives the source through 50 Ω and reads the drain across a 50 Ω load. Insertion loss is 20 log of the output with the switch over the output without it. Both leads are coaxial with grounded shields.

operation.text: ADG733: three SPDT switches in a 16-lead TSSOP or QSOP. ADG734: four SPDT switches in a 20-lead TSSOP. Each switch connects its drain D to one of two sources, A or B. Signals pass both ways and may swing from VSS to VDD.

Operation runs from 1.8 V to 5.5 V on one supply, or from ±2.5 V. Full specifications are given at 5 V and 3 V single supply and at ±2.5 V. On a single supply VSS goes to ground near the chip. Supply current is around 1 nA static and rises with logic switching frequency (TPC 13).

On the ADG733 the address bits A0, A1 and A2 each pick the side of switches 1, 2 and 3: a 0 closes the A side, a 1 the B side. EN is active low; with EN high every switch is open. The ADG734 has one input per switch, IN1 to IN4: a 0 closes the B side, a 1 the A side. Inputs are TTL and CMOS compatible; at 5 V, VINH is 2.4 V min and VINL 0.8 V max.
Each switch opens the closed side before it closes the other, so the two sources are never joined during a change. The gap is 13 ns typical at 5 V, at least 1 ns over temperature.

RON is 2.5 Ω typ at 5 V, 6 Ω typ at 3 V and 2.5 Ω typ at ±2.5 V. Channels match within 0.4 Ω max, and across the signal range RON varies by 0.5 Ω typ at 5 V. RON peaks in mid-range and grows as the supply falls (TPC 1) and as temperature rises (TPC 3 to TPC 5).
Internal diodes clamp overvoltage on the A, EN, IN, S and D pins. The current through them must stay within the absolute maximum ratings: 30 mA continuous on an analog or digital input.

The part is sensitive to electrostatic discharge: charges up to 4000 V can build up on people and test gear and discharge unnoticed. It has built-in ESD protection, but high-energy discharges can still damage it, so it needs ESD handling.
